title: Root Down the Tallest Stack
statement:
You get an array stacks, where stacks[i] is the number of coins in stack i, and an integer k.

Do the following k times: pick the stack with the most coins (any one of them if several tie) and shrink it to the integer square root of its size, floor(√size). The removed coins are gone.

Return the total number of coins left in all stacks after the k rounds.

examples.why: Round 1 shrinks 30 to 5. Round 2 picks the 10 and leaves 3. The stacks are [5, 4, 3].
16 → 4, then 4 is still the tallest and becomes 2, then one of the two 2s becomes 1. The same stack can be picked again, so shrinking each stack once is wrong.
The root of 1 is 1, so extra rounds change nothing.

hints: Each round needs the current largest stack. What structure gives you the maximum quickly, again and again, while values change?
A max-heap: pop the top, push back its square root. k rounds cost O(k log n).
Once the top of the heap is 1, every stack is 1 and you can stop early.

explain.intuition:
The rule "always the biggest" is the signature of a priority queue. Scanning the whole array for the maximum in every round costs O(n) per round, which is 1010 operations at the limits. A max-heap hands over the biggest stack in O(log n) and takes the shrunken stack back in O(log n).

A shrunk stack can still be the biggest, as in [16, 2], so it has to go back into the same heap rather than being set aside.
steps: Put every stack size into a max-heap.
Repeat k times: pop the largest value v, push floor(√v). Stop early if v is 1.
Return the sum of the heap's values.
pitfalls: Shrinking each stack at most once, or going through them in sorted order once. A stack can be picked again.
Taking the square root with floating point and rounding up. You need the floor; Math.floor(Math.sqrt(v)) is exact for values up to 109, and Python has math.isqrt.
Summing into a 32-bit integer. 10<sup>5</sup> stacks of 10<sup>9</sup> coins is 10<sup>14</sup>.

solutions.title: Scan for the maximum each round
solutions.idea: Find the largest stack by scanning, replace it by its root, repeat k times.

solutions.title: Max-heap
solutions.idea: Keep all stacks in a max-heap. Each round pops the biggest and pushes its root back.

followups: k can be 10¹⁸. Each stack can only be rooted about five times before it reaches 1. How does that bound the real work?
Return the order in which stack indexes were picked, breaking ties by the smaller index.
